Interface IuRefreshableCacheConfiguration

public interface IuRefreshableCacheConfiguration
Provides runtime tuning parameters to a IuRefreshableCache.

All methods supply a default, so an implementation only overrides the values it needs to change. The cache reads one configuration snapshot for each operation, allowing a supplier to expose current values without recreating the cache. The defensive call cache is short-lived by design: refresh TTL should be short enough that callers see reasonably current data from a stable backing source; cache TTL should be no longer than PT30M; and call TTL should be short.

Values are validated by the invocation that reads them, so an invalid value fails that invocation and leaves the cache intact. See IuRefreshableCache for what each value controls, when a change takes effect, and how the values trade off against one another.

  • Method Details

    • getRefreshTtl

      default Duration getRefreshTtl()
      Gets the interval after which a cached result becomes stale and the next caller triggers a refresh.

      This is the staleness bound under healthy conditions: a value older than this is still served immediately, but triggers a background refresh. A change applies to entries already cached, in both directions, without discarding them, because staleness is evaluated against the interval in effect when an entry is read.

      Returns null to disable the defensive call cache entirely, in which case every invocation results in a remote call and getCacheTtl() is not used.

      Returns:
      refresh interval; null to disable caching. Must be positive when non-null.

    • getCacheTtl

      default Duration getCacheTtl()
      Gets the maximum length of time a cached result remains available once it has stopped being refreshed successfully.

      The interval between getRefreshTtl() and this value is the downstream service outage tolerance window: a successful refresh restarts the window, so a healthy entry never expires.

      This value also bounds how long a queued invalidation hint is retained, and therefore how much work each cached lookup performs when evaluating pending invalidations. A long cache TTL combined with a high rate of invalidating calls is the combination to avoid.

      A change applies as each entry is stored, so an entry already cached takes the new value at its next successful refresh rather than immediately.

      Returns:
      short-term cache time to live; should be no longer than PT30M and must be longer than getRefreshTtl()

    • getCallTtl

      default Duration getCallTtl()
      Gets the maximum length of time to wait for a remote call to complete.

      Applies to a caller waiting on an uncached value and to a background refresh alike: a refresh still in flight after this interval is cancelled and replaced, so a hung call cannot block every later refresh for its key, nor occupy a thread indefinitely.

      Returns:
      short call timeout; must be positive

    • getThreads

      default int getThreads()
      Gets the number of threads available for performing remote calls.

      Changing this value, or getPending(), replaces the call pool; the replaced pool is shut down gracefully so calls already in flight run to completion. Idle threads time out, so an idle cache holds no threads.

      Returns:
      thread count; must be positive

    • getPending

      default int getPending()
      Gets the maximum number of remote calls that may be queued while all threads are busy.

      A full queue rejects the dispatch. For a key that already holds a value that is absorbed — the stale value is served instead — so this value acts as a load-shedding control as well as a resource bound: too tight converts pressure into staleness, too loose converts it into latency.

      Returns:
      pending queue size; must be positive
